The Green asymptotic is proved directly by finite-support Fourier and tilting estimates. The first-moment occupation identity gives the stated critical branching-random-walk interpretation; percolation transfer is not inferred.
Path splitting gives submultiplicativity, the block decomposition proves the connective-constant limit, and the root test plus its infimum formula locate susceptibility divergence.
High-dimensional coefficient, mean-square and functional limits are explicitly cited lace-expansion inputs. Splitting the two generating series proves their stated Abelian consequences.

The cited critical spatial theorem and the proved walk equivalent give two-sided global comparison after adjusting finitely many sites. Nonnegative convolution comparison and the discounted Fourier argument give every diagram threshold. The existing triangle theorem supplies the stated mean-field bounds.
Markov composition and Tonelli give the binomial time weights; summing transition bounds proves the spatial order and each strict dimensional threshold. Strong Markov gives hitting probabilities.

The stable local limit controls intermediate times; the cited bound controls early and late times. Gaussian inversion of the fractional resolvent gives the constant; holding normalization is checked exactly.
Truncated covariance fixes the logarithmic symbol constant. The Fourier L1 argument uses a growing inner region and a separate intermediate-frequency bound.
Markov time composition gives every potential. The local limit controls intermediate times; early times use the cited off-diagonal bound. At equality the leading contribution is from n≥|x|².

The cited critical percolation equivalent gives global two-sided Green comparison after finite-set adjustment. Ordered nonnegative convolution transfers the spatial orders and critical triangle finiteness.
Normalizes the all-lattice law and mixture, proves cube irreducibility and aperiodicity, and separates the marginal analytic obligations from the alpha-not-two provenance.

The general covariance change of variables, localized Fourier remainder bound and directional fourth Gaussian derivative yield the Green correction. The occupation identity supplies only the expected branching-walk interpretation.
Exact uniform-coordinate moments determine the angular term and its sign; removing the holding atom uses the exact Green normalization identity.

Fourier inversion and a radial cutoff give the leading coefficients. Monotone comparison of the resolvent deficit transfers the radial calculation to an asymptotically isotropic symbol without a holding assumption.
The uniform symbol error bounds the difference of resolvent deficits. Expanding the logarithmic cutoff gives the next term, and an integrable subtraction gives the two-dimensional finite part.

Markov time composition gives the discounted potential. The uniform local limit controls intermediate times, the cited transition estimate controls early times, and the discounted local-limit bound controls late times.

The critical local limit is uniform for all times beyond the square of the separation. Replacing geometric discounting by a time cutoff has a uniformly lower-order error; integration gives the surviving fraction. C9HG gives the refined compact-profile ratio.

A telescoping sum reduces relative errors to a uniformly small multiple of the full potential plus finitely many lower-order translates. CEVT verifies that these translates are negligible for the clipped marginal law.

The cited critical percolation equivalent gives the limiting ratio to the walk Green function. The transfer criterion raises that ratio to the convolution order, and CEVT supplies the exact spatial coefficients.
